talk: Payback period is how long an investment takes to earn back what it cost. It's the simplest test there is: how long until I'm back to even? Shorter is safer, because the future is never certain.

terms.meaning: Time until an investment has earned back its cost.
What you pay at the start.
What the investment brings in or saves each year.

questions.prompt: New LED floodlights cost $240,000 and cut the power bill by $60,000 a year. What's the payback period?
whyNot: After 2 years you've saved 2 x $60,000 = $120,000. That's only half the cost.
After 5 years you've saved 5 x $60,000 = $300,000, more than the cost. You were back to even a year earlier.
After 6 years you've saved 6 x $60,000 = $360,000. You got your money back well before that.

questions.prompt: A new big screen costs $300,000. It brings in $50,000 a year in adverts but costs $10,000 a year to run. What's the payback period?
questions.hint: Use what it earns after running costs.
whyNot: $300,000 / $50,000 = 6 years forgets the $10,000 a year it costs to run.
$300,000 / $10,000 = 30 years divides by the running cost. Divide by what it actually earns you each year.

questions.prompt: Two projects cost $100,000 each. Project A pays $50,000 a year for 2 years, then nothing. Project B pays $25,000 a year for 8 years. Which is true?
options: A pays back faster, B earns more
A pays back faster and earns more
B pays back faster, A earns more
questions.hint: Work out payback and total for each.
working: A: $100,000 / $50,000 = 2 years to pay back, and 2 x $50,000 = $100,000 in total. You just get your money back.
B: $100,000 / $25,000 = 4 years to pay back, and 8 x $25,000 = $200,000 in total.
Payback only tells you how fast. It ignores everything after.
whyNot: A pays back faster, but it stops at $100,000, exactly what you put in. B earns $200,000.
B takes 4 years to pay back, twice as long as A. It does earn more in total, though.
Same cost, very different shape. A is quick and then stops. B is slow but keeps paying.

takeaway: Payback tells you how fast you're back to even. It says nothing about what comes after.
